Federal Judge Mark Pittman is seeking to understand any agreements that may have led to a Musk-owned company withdrawing its antitrust claims against Apple. Here are the details.

Judge orders look into any settlement with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple from a lawsuit they brought last year against Apple and OpenAI, with prejudice.

According to the original complaint, Apple and OpenAI were accused of conspiring to prevent competing AI apps from gaining exposure on the App Store, due to a deal to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence. Apple and OpenAI have denied the allegations.

In their filing earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI only stated that they had "resolved the claims against Apple in this lawsuit," and emphasised that they did not seek to withdraw claims against OpenAI.

First reported by POLITICO, Judge Mark Pittman, who has been presiding over the case, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit to the court "any agreement or series of agreements with Apple to resolve the claims against Apple by Plaintiffs in this case."

The order comes in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI, seeking to compel X and SpaceXAI to make public their settlement with Apple. Pittman has also ordered the two companies to respond to OpenAI's motion by noon on September 17.
